RE: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Taylor Kimura
Member ID: W354999576
Reference Number: POC-37F3AA304D-16940
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-07-31
Requested Service: Hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914
Treating Surgeon: Okafor, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31 (Reference Number POC-37F3AA304D-16940). This appeal is being submitted within the 180-day window identified in that notice (by 2027-01-27), consistent with Cigna's published appeal policy, which states that a member should "call customer service at the telephone number on your ID card within 180 calendar days of the date of the initial payment or denial notice" to begin the appeal process. I am submitting this written appeal along with supporting clinical documentation.

**Stated Reason for Denial**

The notice states that the request was denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal to supply the complete clinical record and to demonstrate that the documentation, taken as a whole, addresses the medical-necessity elements applicable to this procedure.

**Applicable Policy**

I understand that Cigna's medical necessity review for hip arthroscopic procedures, including CPT 29914, is governed by the eviCore/Cigna guideline titled "CMM-314: Hip Surgery – Arthroscopic and Open Procedures." I have been able to directly verify the text of the section titled "Arthroscopic or Open Hip Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI)" in the version of CMM-314 effective August 1, 2024. I have not been able to obtain the full text of the FAI-specific criteria in the most recent posted version of CMM-314 (effective March 7, 2026), so where I quote policy language below, I am quoting the August 1, 2024 version. I respectfully request that Cigna confirm whether the criteria in the version applied to this determination differ from the language quoted here, and if so, provide that language so the record can be supplemented accordingly.

The August 1, 2024 version of CMM-314 states, under "Arthroscopic or Open Hip Surgery for Femoroacetabular Impingement (FAI) Indications":

"Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:
 Imaging shows BOTH of the following findings:
  FAI confirmation with X-ray, MRI, or CT showing ANY of the following findings: Alpha angle greater than 50 degrees; Pistol-grip deformity; Decrease of femoral head-neck offset; Acetabular retroversion (i.e., crossover sign, ischial spine sign); Coxa profunda
  Presence of Tönnis grade 0-1 osteoarthritis
 Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings:
  Positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation)
  Limited passive hip internal rotation
 Symptoms include groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and significantly limits activities
 Unresponsive to at least three (3) months of provider-directed non-surgical treatment which must include the following (unless contraindicated):
  An image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid) to which there was a positive response (i.e., any degree of pain reduction achieved within 2 weeks after the injection)"

And under "Non-Indications":

"Arthroscopic or open hip surgery for femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered not medically necessary for ANY other indication, condition, or when ANY of the following radiographic findings are present on plain x-ray: Joint space narrowing <2mm along the sourcil; Presence of Tönnis [grade 2-3 osteoarthritis]" [text of this exclusion was truncated in the source document I retrieved; I am not able to quote it in full and am not asserting the missing words].

**How the Clinical Record Addresses Each Element**

1. **Imaging findings.** MRI arthrogram of the hip dated 2026-06-24 documents an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees (above the 50-degree threshold referenced in the policy language quoted above). The same study documents joint space preserved and Tönnis grade 0, which is within the Tönnis grade 0-1 range referenced in the policy language quoted above.

2. **Physical exam findings.** The exam documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, consistent with the anterior impingement sign and limited passive internal rotation referenced in the policy language quoted above. [The exam note does not appear to separately label the finding as "anterior impingement sign" or specify "limited passive hip internal rotation" in those exact words; if the treating surgeon's documentation supports these specific labels, an updated exam note or addendum from Dr. Okafor confirming this terminology is attached/being requested.]

3. **Symptoms and functional impact.** The record documents 14 months of progressive hip pain unrelieved by rest, with sharp anterior groin pain on sitting and pivoting, and inability to run or squat. This corresponds to the "groin-dominant hip pain that is worsened by flexion (e.g., squatting or prolonged sitting) and significantly limits activities" language quoted above.

4. **Conservative treatment.** The record documents:
   - 16 weeks (2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15) of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 24 visits completed, per the physical therapy discharge note;
   - NSAID therapy for 4 months with inadequate relief;
   - A corticosteroid injection administered 2026-03-21, documented to have provided 4 weeks of partial relief.
   This exceeds the three-month minimum period of provider-directed non-surgical treatment referenced in the policy language quoted above, and includes an injection with a documented partial response. [The injection note does not specify whether it was image-guided or whether the injectate included a local anesthetic in addition to corticosteroid; if that detail is not already in the chart, an addendum from the administering provider confirming the injection technique and any anesthetic used is attached/being requested, since the policy language quoted above specifies "an image-guided intra-articular hip injection with local anesthetic (with or without corticosteroid)."]

5. **Absence of disqualifying findings.** The MRI arthrogram documents Tönnis grade 0 and preserved joint space, which does not meet the Tönnis grade 2-3 exclusion referenced in the policy language quoted above (to the extent that exclusion applies; as noted above, I was not able to retrieve the complete wording of that exclusion). The record also documents no active infection and no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

**Conclusion**

Based on the clinical documentation summarized above — including the imaging findings, exam findings, symptom history, and documented conservative treatment — I respectfully request that Cigna reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) as recommended by Dr. Okafor. If any specific element of the record remains unclear or insufficient in Cigna's view, I ask that Cigna identify that specific element in writing so that it can be promptly supplemented, consistent with Cigna's own appeal guidance that "[a]long with your written appeal request... include any documentation that supports your argument."

Please notify me and Dr. Okafor's office in writing of the outcome of this appeal. I also request confirmation of the exact version and full text of the CMM-314 (or successor) guideline criteria applied to this specific determination, including its effective date, so that the record can address that language directly if it differs from the version quoted in this letter.

Enclosed/Attached:
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-07-31 (Reference POC-37F3AA304D-16940)
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-23 to 2026-06-15)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-03-21)
- MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-24
- Clinic/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range of motion
- [Any additional physician statement or addendum from Dr. Okafor, if obtained]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this appeal.

Sincerely,

Taylor Kimura
